title: Project
description: A GrooveKit project (song.json). Times are integer ticks at 960 PPQ unless a field says otherwise.

schemaVersion.description: 4 since sampler layers follow the keys played by default (3: playlist tracks are numbered lanes and audio clips play sampler channels). Older songs are converted when they open.

key.description: The song's key, e.g. "A minor" or "F# major": melodies taken from humming or reference tracks move into it, and samples are matched against it.

swing.description: Delays every second 16th note by up to half a 16th (1: a dotted-16th feel). Applies to pattern notes that start on an off-beat 16th.

Id.description: Stable identifier, unique within its collection.

Ticks.description: Position in ticks (960 per quarter note).

TickLength.description: Duration in ticks (960 per quarter note).

Pan.description: -1 is hard left, 0 centre, 1 hard right.

Lane.description: Playlist track number, 0 at the top. Any clip can go on any track, and a track needs no setting up first.

Channel.description: A channel-rack entry: one instrument whose output feeds a mixer insert.

solo.description: While any channel is soloed, only soloed channels play.

group.description: Which list of the channel rack shows the channel: rack for sounds played by patterns, arrangement for samples dropped onto the playlist. Only the view depends on it.

SamplerInstrument.description: Built-in polyphonic sampler. Every layer whose key and velocity range match a note plays it; audio clips on the playlist play its first layer.

polyphony.description: Maximum simultaneous voices; the oldest voice is stolen.

filter.description: Filters every voice and audio clip, after the layer's volume envelope.

SamplerFilter.description: A resonant filter per voice (and per audio clip), its cutoff moved by its own envelope.

type.description: lowpass and highpass are 12 dB/octave, lowpass24 and highpass24 steeper at 24; bandpass keeps a band around the cutoff, notch takes it out.

resonance.description: 0 is a gentle slope; towards 1 the cutoff rings.

envelopeAmount.description: Octaves the envelope moves the cutoff at its peak; negative moves it down.

envelope.description: Shape of the cutoff movement; sustain is the share of the amount held.

SamplerModulation.description: Envelopes and LFOs that move a sampler's volume, cutoff, resonance, pan and pitch over each note. Notes only: audio clips keep the layer's volume envelope and the filter's cutoff envelope. Amounts are shares of each target's span: volume all of it, cutoff 5 octaves, resonance all of it, pan from centre to one side, pitch 24 semitones.

volume.description: Tremolo; the volume envelope is each layer's own.

cutoff.description: Moves the filter's cutoff; its envelope is the filter's own (envelope and envelopeAmount).

pitch.description: An envelope amount of 0.5 drops or raises the pitch by 12 semitones, as in a pitched-down kick.

envelope.description: Its shape; the amount sets how far it moves the target at its peak.

amount.description: Share of the target's span the envelope moves it at its peak; negative moves it the other way, 0 is off.

Lfo.description: A low-frequency oscillator added to the target.

amount.description: Share of the target's span it swings either way; 0 is off.

speed.description: Cycles a second, when not synced.

sync.description: Beats per cycle (0.25 is a 16th, 4 a bar in 4/4) following the tempo, instead of speed.

delay.description: Seconds after a note starts before it moves.

attack.description: Seconds it then takes to swing fully.

retrigger.description: Each note starts its cycle; false keeps one cycle running for every note.

sample.description: Audio file path, absolute or relative to the project folder.

rootKey.description: Key at which the sample plays at its original pitch.

pitchTracking.description: If false, every key plays the sample at root pitch (drums).

transpose.description: Semitones. Audio clips are pitch-shifted and keep their length.

mode.description: oneShot plays to the end of the sample and ignores note-off; gate releases on note-off.

envelope.description: Volume over each note. Over an audio clip, the attack starts where the clip starts and the release ends where it ends.

start.description: Seconds into the file where the part that plays begins.

end.description: Seconds into the file where the part that plays ends; unset is the file's end.

reverse.description: Plays the part between start and end backwards.

loop.description: Notes only. forward loops the part that plays, pingPong plays it back and forth; a looping layer plays until its note ends, then releases.

fadeIn.description: Seconds the part that plays fades in over (notes only).

fadeOut.description: Seconds it fades out over before its end (notes only; not while looping).

normalize.description: Brings the part that plays up (or down) to a peak of 0 dB before its gain (notes only).

punch.description: Transient shaping (notes only): positive sharpens each hit's attack, negative softens it.

tail.description: Transient shaping (notes only): positive brings up what rings on after each hit, negative tightens it.

sourceTempo.description: Tempo the file was recorded at. When set, audio clips playing the layer are time-stretched (pitch kept) to the project tempo. Notes ignore it.

Grains.description: Granular playback (notes only): the part plays as short overlapping grains read at the note's pitch, while a playhead moves through it at its own speed, so pitch and timing are apart: a higher key sounds higher but no faster, and a slower speed stretches the sound without lowering it. Few, short grains leave space between them (stutter, texture); many long ones are smooth.

on.description: Plays the layer as grains; off (the default) plays the sample straight, pitch and speed together, and keeps the other settings.

speed.description: How fast the playhead moves through the part: 1 its own pace, 0.5 half (twice as long), 0 holds still (a held texture until the note ends), 2 twice as fast.

spray.description: Seconds grains scatter around the playhead, at random: smears and blurs.

detune.description: Random detuning of each grain, up to this many cents either way: thickens.

width.description: How widely grains are spread in stereo, 0 to 1.

shape.description: Each grain's rise and fall: smooth, flat (fuller, more of the sound) or pluck (struck, then dying away).

Envelope.description: Delay, attack, hold, decay, sustain, release. Times in seconds; sustain is a level from 0 to 1. The curves bend the attack, decay and release: 0 is straight, positive moves fast at first and then eases (the way sounds fade), negative starts slowly.

PluginRef.description: A hosted VST3 or AU plugin.

state.description: Path of the saved state blob, relative to the project folder.

params.description: Parameter id or name to normalized value (0..1), applied after the state.

Pattern.description: Notes for any number of channels. A pattern clip plays all of them.

length.description: Loop length. If absent, the end of the last note rounded up to a whole bar.

tracks.description: Settings of tracks 0, 1, 2 and so on; tracks past the end of the list have the defaults.

PlaylistTrack.description: A playlist lane. Tracks only arrange: how clips sound is set by their channels and the mixer.

solo.description: While any track is soloed, only soloed tracks play.

PatternClip.description: Plays a pattern, repeating it every pattern length until the clip ends.

offset.description: Ticks into the pattern where the clip starts playing.

channel.description: The sampler channel whose first layer the clip plays, with the channel's settings and routing.

offset.description: Seconds into the layer's part of the file (from its start, or from its end when reversed) where playback starts.

AutomationClip.description: Drives one parameter. A target follows the points of all its unmuted clips; before the first point it holds the first value, after a clip it holds that clip's last value until the next point. Points past the clip's length are ignored.

AutomationTarget.description: What an automation clip drives. channel: param is volume or pan; for samplers also filterCutoff (Hz), filterResonance (0..1) or filterEnvelopeAmount (octaves); for plugin instruments also a parameter id or name (normalized 0..1). insert: volume or pan. effect: the effect's parameter id or mix (for plugins: id or name, normalized 0..1). send: level.

value.description: In the parameter's own units (dB for volume and send level, -1..1 for pan).

curve.description: Shape of the segment to the next point: 0 linear, negative ease-in, positive ease-out.

Mixer.description: Mixer inserts. The insert with id "master" is required and is the final output.

solo.description: While any insert is soloed, only soloed inserts are heard, with the inserts feeding them and the ones they feed.

output.description: Insert this one feeds. Ignored on master.

mix.description: How much of the effect is heard: 0 is the signal as it comes in, 1 only the effect's output (delay-compensated, so it works for any effect). Automatable as the effect parameter "mix".

params.description: Parameter id to value, in the units of the effect catalogue (groovekit-engine effects). Unlisted parameters keep their defaults.

mix.description: How much of the effect is heard: 0 is the signal as it comes in, 1 only the effect's output (delay-compensated, so it works for any effect). Automatable as the effect parameter "mix".
